meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided, and on what basis?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.

Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and I have Turnitin's own guide in my bag saying its indicator should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student. Your school's procedure 4.3 says the same thing: software alone does not establish a concern. So was Owen heard before you entered that zero, or did the machine decide for you?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My child never lies, so are you calling me a liar too? I'm writing down that you said "your son cheated" with nothing but software in front of you, and I'm going to the principal's office when we're done here. Very reliable is an adjective, Hale, not evidence.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

You're threatening my son's record because his mother asked a question? Read your own procedure, Hale: 4.4 says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing goes on file, and 4.5 is for repeated concerns. Put that threat in an email to me today, and I'll take it to the principal and then to the board under section 42.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay be withdrawn, that you apologise for entering it before anyone spoke to him or called me, and that nothing about this is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record, and the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4 was never reached because no evidence beyond the detector score was offered.
What moved her: Nothing, because every turn offered a software score, an accusation, or a threat instead of a dated document she could check.
What cost ground: Threatening to put it on his permanent record if she kept fighting, because that hit her one non-negotiable and contradicted the school's own procedure for a first concern.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never came near that night, since only the detector score was put forward; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: In your first reply, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then put something dated from Owen's own work in front of her that she can check herself, instead of leading with the detector score.
